I’ll check how server-info requests are routed and add separate request capacity while preserving the response and public access. I’ll use the repository’s Python style skill for the code and tests.
Server-info currently runs through the Flask bridge and shares its worker capacity with other requests. I’ll give both server-info paths a dedicated concurrency limiter in that bridge. This keeps the existing handler, authentication rules, response, and Gunicorn/Waitress behavior intact.
The change is in place. I also found that basic-auth still required credentials for server-info, so I added an exact-path public-access exception for both routes, including the configured static prefix. The regression test holds the shared worker capacity occupied and checks that unauthenticated server-info requests still return the same bytes as the Flask response.
The saturation tests and all eight existing server-info handler tests passed. Two test-environment issues surfaced: the broad auth test module needs the missing `jwt` package, and pytest’s summary hook hits a sandbox restriction. I’ll keep the auth regression in the lightweight auth test module and disable only the summary hook for the final run; no dependencies will be installed.
Implemented dedicated worker capacity for both server-info paths, so shared-pool exhaustion no longer blocks capability discovery.

Public access works with custom static prefixes. The existing Flask handler preserves response content and Gunicorn/Waitress behavior.

Added saturation, response-equivalence, and authentication regression coverage. All 16 targeted tests passed. No dependencies installed; no full suite run.
